title: Morphological Analysis of Pig Vagus Nerve Using Image Processing
author: Nicole A. Pelot
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6bvhan6
materials: We used Nikon's NIS Elements software (v5.02.01, Build 1270) to segment pig vagus nerve micrographs stained with Masson's trichrome using the General Analysis RGB tool.
We used Nikon's NIS Elements software (v5.02.01, Build 1270) to segment pig vagus nerve micrographs stained with Masson's trichrome using the General Analysis RGB tool.

steps.title: Convert Segmented Images to Graticule Masks
steps.instruction: Convert the binary segmented image into Graticule Masks and save them as TIF files.

steps.title: Extract Pixel Coordinates
steps.instruction: Import the TIF files into Matlab and use the bwboundaries function to generate a data structure of the x and y coordinates of the pixels for each closed boundary of the loaded binary images.

steps.title: Scale Pixel Coordinates
steps.instruction: Scale the pixel coordinates to microns using the segmented scale bar.

steps.title: Perform Image Preprocessing
steps.instruction: Select and apply preprocessing steps for each image, such as smoothing and sharpening.

steps.title: Identify Nerve and Endoneurium
steps.instruction: Select ranges of hues, saturations, and intensities for each image to identify the endoneurium (fascicles) and the entirety of the nerve.

steps.title: Perform Image Postprocessing
steps.instruction: Apply postprocessing steps to each image to refine the target areas.

substeps.instruction: Set a minimum size criterion to eliminate small off-target regions

steps.title: Manually Adjust Target Regions
steps.instruction: Perform manual adjustments as needed to ensure accuracy.

substeps.instruction: Fill target areas that were not captured

steps.title: Calculate Morphological Measurements
steps.instruction: Calculate the cross-sectional area and effective diameter of each fascicle and nerve using Matlab.

substeps.instruction: Use Matlab's polyarea function to calculate the cross-sectional area
Determine the effective diameter by calculating the diameter of a circle with the same cross-sectional area as the raw trace
